governments_checked: Eureka County (no zoning ordinance; no incorporated municipalities; the unincorporated towns of Eureka and Crescent Valley have town code titles with no zoning)
sources_checked: code: Eureka County Code (July 2018 edition) Title 8 Planning Commission, Title 9 Natural Resource and Land Use, Title 4 Licenses Permits and Taxes, Title 12 Town of Eureka, Title 13 Town of Crescent Valley, Title 1, and the Index of Sections, PDFs downloaded and searched for solar, wind, renewable, energy, battery, storage, moratorium and zoning (https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/departments/county-code/); ordinance: separately posted ordinances on the same page (2017 marijuana establishments, 2018 and 2026 room tax, 2026 holiday leave resolution) reviewed by title; minutes: Board of County Commissioners minutes, 134 PDFs, downloaded and searched for the same words (https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/departments/commissioners/commission-meeting-minutes/, 2022-01 to 2026-09-15); agendas: Board of County Commissioners agenda and backup packets, 21 PDFs (https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/departments/commissioners/commission-meeting-agendas/, 2026-01-06 to 2026-10-06); minutes: Planning Commission minutes posted on its page, 2023-05-01 and 2023-08-30, the only ones online (https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/business-development/eureka-county-planning-commission/); docket: PUCN renewable docket list searched for Eureka, finding 20-06014 (Nevada Gold Energy TS Solar, 200 MW, UEPA permit) with its document list opened and 25-01035 (BRP Sandstone 3, Eureka Transmission Project notice) (https://pucweb1.state.nv.us/puc2/Dktinfo.aspx?Util=Renewable, 2020 to 2025); news search: web searches for Eureka County Nevada solar, wind, renewable energy, ordinance and moratorium (2024 to 2026)
note: No zoning: the 2026 Multi-Jurisdictional Hazard Mitigation Plan in the 2026-06-18 BOCC backup says "Eureka County has not adopted a zoning ordinance." The Nevada Gold Energy RETA application (https://www.energy.nv.gov/uploadedFiles/energynvgov/content/Programs/Nevada%20Gold%20Energy%20LLC%20RETA_Redacted.pdf, opened) lists county permits as "None. Eureka County has not adopted a zoning ordinance or building permit requirement for this portion of Eureka County." What the code does set: subdivision and parcel map rules, planned unit development, flood plain management, mobile home rules, water rights dedication, and Title 9 ch. 30, which adopts the Natural Resources and Land Use Plan (master plan policies, not siting standards). Policy, not a restriction: the BOCC on 2023-02-21 (minutes pp. 10-14, opened) adopted a Resolution Restating and Summarizing Policies Related to Alternative Energy Siting and Development. It says the county "generally does not support large wind energy projects", prefers disturbed lands, supports agrisolar on irrigated lands, generally opposes tax abatements and supports bonding. It sets no ban, moratorium, setback, height, noise or size limit. Also on record: in 2022-10 the board recommended denying a RETA tax abatement for the TS Solar project; in 2024-02-20 the Stagecoach Wind application (55,000 acres, Newark Valley) was reported withdrawn; in 2026-06 and 2026-09 staff reported solar proposals in Diamond Valley (Balanced Rock Power open house 2026-10-20). BLM Western Solar Plan exclusion areas on federal land are federal, not county, rules. Could not be searched: BOCC minutes of 2025-02-04, 2025-02-18, 2025-03-04 and 2025-03-18 are image-only PDFs with no text layer; Planning Commission minutes of 2023-05-01 are image-only; Planning Commission minutes other than 2023-05-01 and 2023-08-30 are not posted (the commission reviews land divisions only). The PUCN 20-06014 docket document list was opened, but the filed documents themselves were not. Review: ACCEPT. Section 2 checked source by source, 2026-10-13. (1) Governments (section 1): no incorporated municipality. The Census 2024 Gazetteer lists Eureka and Crescent Valley only as CDPs (FUNCSTAT S, GEOIDs 3223900 and 3216300). data/census_governments_2024.csv lists 19 Nevada places with FUNCSTAT A and none in 32011. The towns of Eureka and Crescent Valley are unincorporated towns governed by County Code Titles 12 and 13, which hold no zoning (searched). governments_checked is complete. (2) No zoning (primary_law): I re-opened https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/departments/county-code/ and downloaded every posted file (Titles 1 to 19, Index of Sections July 2018, table of contents, citation list, and the four separately posted ordinances; 28 PDFs), a wider set than the drafter searched. I searched them for solar, wind, renewable, battery, energy storage, moratorium, turbine, photovoltaic, zoning and zone. Energy hits were only aviation turbine fuel (Title 4), building-code wind speed (Title 6 ch. 140, the adopted International Building Code, a building code that is not counted) and 'renewable and nonrenewable resources' in Title 9 definitions. 'Zoning' appears only in Title 8 ch. 130 flood plain management. Title 8 is subdivision, parcel map, large parcel, PUD, flood, mobile home and water rights dedication rules; nothing sets energy siting standards. The county states in its own documents that it has no zoning: the 2026 Hazard Mitigation Plan in the 2026-06-18 BOCC packet (p. text line 3904, 'Eureka County has not adopted a zoning ordinance'); the 2010 Master Plan (https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/media/hadfzj4u/master_plan_final-_2010.pdf, opened: 'Zoning has not been adopted within the County', 'Eureka County does not use zoning to regulate land use'; its only energy text is policies encouraging wind, solar and geothermal); the 2024-12-03 BOCC minutes ('Because Eureka County has no permitting or zoning the company does not have to formally file anything', about an inquiry for a wind project); the 2026-06-18 minutes reprinted in the 2026-07-21 packet (District Attorney: 'the County has no zoning, land use regulation or building permits'); and 2026-05-19 packet appraisals ('There is no zoning in Eureka County'). I re-opened the RETA application (https://www.energy.nv.gov/siteassets/content/programs/Nevada_Gold_Energy_LLC_RETA_Redacted.pdf, redirected from the drafter's URL); it reads 'None. Eureka County has not adopted a zoning ordinance or building permit requirement for this portion of Eureka County.' (3) Minutes and agendas (proceeding): re-opened https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/departments/commissioners/commission-meeting-minutes/ (138 linked PDFs, 2022-01 to 2026-09-15, including liquor board, DGGID and RTC minutes) and downloaded all of them. pdftotext plus OCR found no moratorium in any of them and no solar, wind or storage ordinance. Image-only files I OCR'd with tesseract (200 dpi): BOCC 2025-02-04 (16 pp), 2025-02-18 (14 pp), 2025-03-04 (11 pp) and 2025-03-18 (14 pp), and Planning Commission 2023-05-01 (2 pp). The OCR shows only a Mountain Solar NEPA kickoff and solar projects raising assessed values (2025-02-04); the PC minutes note only 'various email requests for zoning and permitting information'. So the drafter's image-only gap is now closed. Spot-checked in full: 2023-02-21 (pp. 10-14). The 'Resolution Restating and Summarizing Policies Related to Alternative Energy Siting and Development' reads 'Eureka County generally does not support large wind energy projects' and lists policies on disturbed lands, agrisolar, tax abatements, bonding and federal coordination. It has no ban, moratorium, setback, height, noise, size or district rule, so it is not a section 3 restriction (it is an opposition signal the note rightly records). Also read 2022-09-20 and 2022-10-20 (RETA denial recommendation), 2023-04-20 (abatement granted; Stagecoach Wind cooperating-agency MOU), 2023-10-03 (Stagecoach segregation notice), 2024-02-20 (Stagecoach withdrawn), 2024-12-03, 2026-06-18 and 2026-09-15 (Diamond Valley solar proposals; Balanced Rock Power open house). These match the drafter's note. Agendas: re-opened the agendas page (21 PDFs, 2026-01-06 to 2026-10-06) and searched all packets; the 'moratorium' hits are a state data-center discussion, federal water moratoria and a Medicaid moratorium, and there is no county energy ordinance or moratorium on any agenda through 2026-10-06. I did not reconcile the posted minutes against the full meeting calendar, so one or two meetings may be missing from the posted set. Planning Commission: only 2023-05-01 and 2023-08-30 minutes are posted (https://www.eurekacountynv.gov/business-development/eureka-county-planning-commission/). The page says the commission is advisory and reviews parcel, subdivision and large-parcel maps. With no zoning code, any siting ordinance would have to be adopted by the BOCC and would appear in BOCC agendas and minutes, which are covered. I judge this gap acceptable, but the pass note should state it. (4) PUCN docket: re-opened the renewable docket lists (active and completed, https://pucweb1.state.nv.us/puc2/Dktinfo.aspx?Util=Renewable). Eureka appears only in 20-06014 (TS Solar, Nevada Gold Energy) and 25-01035 (BRP Sandstone 3, Eureka Transmission Project on federal land); no completed docket names Eureka. The 20-06014 document list shows only applicant, staff and Commission filings, with no Eureka County filing. I OCR'd the order (DocID 4148, https://pucweb1.state.nv.us/PDF/AxImages/DOCKETS_2020_THRU_PRESENT/2020-6/4148.pdf, 9 pp, image-only): it grants the UEPA permit on 2020-08-12 with no county condition. 25-01035 shows no documents on the old site (filed after 2023-10). (5) News search: own searches for Eureka County Nevada solar, ordinance, moratorium and zoning found nothing beyond the Eureka Sentinel coverage of the 2026-06-18 meeting (Diamond Valley 500 MW solar proposals). Small corrections for the drafter's row, none affecting acceptance: the minutes page links 138 PDFs, not 134, though the count includes non-BOCC boards; the RETA URL now redirects to /siteassets/content/programs/Nevada_Gold_Energy_LLC_RETA_Redacted.pdf; and the note's 'could not be searched' list is now out of date, because those five files were OCR'd here and contain nothing relevant. The drafter should update the note before the row is recorded. Since that is a change to the note and not to the finding, I accept the check as meeting section 2.
